For any funding amount and any withdrawal value not exceeding it, a successful withdraw(v) called by the owner decreases the contract's balance by exactly v; the mutant instead drains the entire balance, so whenever balance > v the post-state differs.

For any admissible _value v (v < type(uint256).max), after funding c with v+1 wei and the owner calling withdraw(v), c's remaining balance must be exactly 1 wei (P sends only v); the mutant M drains the entire balance v+1, leaving 0 wei.

For any withdrawal value v strictly greater than the contract's (nonzero) balance, C's withdraw(v) must revert (an over-withdrawal is impossible), whereas the mutant drains the whole balance and succeeds for such v.

For any admissible sequence of two withdrawals v1, v2 (each not exceeding the remaining balance) funded with v1+v2+e wei (e>=1), C must end with exactly e wei; the mutant drains the full balance on the first withdrawal, leaving 0.

For any nonzero funded balance b and any withdrawal value v > b, the reference C's withdraw(v) always reverts (an over-withdrawal is impossible), whereas the mutant drains the entire balance and succeeds for such v.
Calling withdraw on c from a non-owner must always revert; only the owner can succeed.
